summary: Describes a framework for the Softwire Hub and Spoke model, where many remote sites (spokes) tunnel through a central concentrator (the hub) using L2TPv2. It spells out the implementation details vendors should follow so their equipment interoperates, supporting IPv4-over-IPv6 and IPv6-over-IPv4 carriage across networks that only run one of the two.

eli5.summary: Imagine a bike wheel: every spoke connects to a central hub. Here, far-away sites each build a private tunnel to one central point, so they can pass messages across a network that speaks a different language.

questions: how to tunnel ipv6 over ipv4 with l2tp
how does l2tpv2 softwire hub and spoke work
how to carry ipv6 over an ipv4 only network with l2tp
what is the softwire initiator and concentrator
subtitle: How an ISP can carry IPv6 over an IPv4-only access network, or IPv4 over IPv6-only, by tunneling every customer to a central hub with L2TPv2.

tldr.problem: A home network may have only IPv4 or only IPv6 on its access link, yet need the other protocol. Vendors also need one agreed way to build the tunnel so their equipment works together.
tldr.mechanism: The customer side (Softwire Initiator) opens an L2TPv2 tunnel with one session to a provider hub (Softwire Concentrator), then runs PPP over it. The PPP link carries the other IP version, and DHCP can add prefixes and DNS.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5571 pins down which L2TPv2 messages, attributes and options a Softwire uses, so that independent implementations interoperate. It reuses existing standards instead of defining a new protocol.

facts.label: Typical PPP MTU on a 1500-byte IPv4 link

today: RFC 5571 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2009, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text itself calls L2TPv2 the phase 1 protocol and says an IKEv2-based approach to securing it should be considered for future phases.

sections.title: The Hub and Spoke Softwire Idea
sections.content:
The Softwires Working Group chose Layer Two Tunneling Protocol version 2 (L2TPv2) as the phase 1 protocol for the Softwire Hub and Spoke solution. A Softwire gives a home network IPv4 across an IPv6-only access network, or IPv6 across an IPv4-only one. The RFC exists so that implementations follow the same details and interoperate.

The customer-side node is the Softwire Initiator (SI). It plays the L2TP Access Concentrator (LAC) client. The provider-side node is the Softwire Concentrator (SC), which plays the L2TP Network Server (LNS). Because the SI starts everything, this is the voluntary tunneling model. The compulsory tunneling model does not apply, so it SHOULD NOT be requested or honored.

A Softwire is made of one L2TPv2 control connection, a single L2TPv2 session, and the PPP link negotiated over that session. Once PPP is up, it carries IP traffic of one address family across the access network of the other. The SI and SC MUST follow RFC 2661 for setup, teardown and OAM.
sections.eli5: The house (spoke) asks the ISP (hub) to open one private tube. Everything of the missing kind, say IPv6 mail on an IPv4-only street, travels inside that tube.

sections.title: How L2TPv2 Meets the Softwire Requirements
sections.content:
The Softwire problem statement ([RFC4925] in the text) lists requirements, and the RFC walks through how L2TPv2 meets each one.

  • NAT traversal: L2TPv2 can run over UDP, so it passes through NAT and NAPT. UDP is always used, because L2TPv2 cannot detect NAT. Replying from a different IP address or UDP port than the request used is NOT RECOMMENDED, since it fails through some NAT filtering behaviors.
  • Scalability: carriers scale by adding more hubs. L2TPv2 is described as widely deployed in broadband services.
  • Routing and multicast: there are no dynamic routing protocols between SC and SI, just a default route from the SI to the SC. Multicast runs transparently.
  • AAA: optional mutual control channel authentication and per-session PPP authentication, integrated with RADIUS, including RADIUS accounting for tunnels (RFC 2867).
  • Privacy and integrity: IPsec ESP can be used on top. Lighter deployments can rely on L2TPv2 channel authentication and PPP authentication.
  • Operations: keepalive HELLO messages and the L2TP MIB (RFC 3371).

Four encapsulations are supported: IPv6/PPP/L2TPv2/UDP/IPv4, IPv4/PPP/L2TPv2/UDP/IPv6, IPv4/PPP/L2TPv2/UDP/IPv4 and IPv6/PPP/L2TPv2/UDP/IPv6.
sections.eli5: The RFC checks L2TPv2 against a to-do list: can it get through home routers, serve millions of homes, prove who is who, and stay alive? Each answer is yes, using tools that already exist.

sections.title: Deployment Scenarios
sections.content:
Four scenarios differ in which home device acts as the SI, and each exists for both IPv6-over-IPv4 (Section 3.1) and IPv4-over-IPv6 (Section 3.2).

  • Host CPE as SI: a dual-stack host connected straight to the modem.
  • Router CPE as SI: a dual-stack customer router, with hosts behind it.
  • Host behind CPE as SI: the CPE only speaks the access network's IP version, and a dual-stack host behind it is the SI.
  • Router behind CPE as SI: same CPE, but a dual-stack router behind it is the SI.

In every scenario, traffic of the access network's own IP version SHOULD NOT traverse the Softwire. Where the SI is a router, it also gets a delegated prefix for the home network. For IPv6, the PPP link uses IPV6CP and the LNS advertises a prefix with a Router Advertisement, while DHCPv6 supplies DNS and any delegated prefix. For IPv4, IPCP gives the SI a global IPv4 address and DNS information, and DHCP can do the same.
sections.eli5: It does not matter whether the tube starts at your computer or at your home router. The only question is who in the house is holding the end of it. The tube still goes to the same hub.

sections.title: Establishing a Softwire
sections.content:
A Softwire is built in three steps, with an optional step 0 for IPsec: (0) an IPsec security association, optionally using IKEv1; (1) an L2TPv2 tunnel with a single session from SI to SC; (2) a PPP session over that L2TPv2 session, after which the SI has an address; (3) optional DHCP for extras such as a delegated prefix and DNS servers.

Only a subset of L2TPv2 is used. The SI always initiates the tunnel and the session, only the incoming call model is allowed, and L2TPv2 packets MUST be carried over UDP. AVPs SHOULD NOT be hidden, since none of them carry sensitive data. The RFC spells out AVP handling: Framing Capabilities and Framing Type SHOULD be ignored by the receiver, and the required (Tx) Connect Speed SHOULD be set to 0 and ignored. Challenge and Challenge Response (tunnel authentication) are OPTIONAL but SHOULD be implemented in the SC. Irrelevant AVPs SHOULD NOT be sent and SHOULD be ignored if received.

On the PPP side, LCP is negotiated and the ACFC option MAY be rejected. Authentication is optional, but if used, CHAP MUST be supported by both ends. IPv6 softwires MUST negotiate IPV6CP, and IPv4 ones MUST negotiate IPCP. For IPv6, the SI MUST send a Router Solicitation after IPV6CP and the SC MUST answer with a Router Advertisement, and Duplicate Address Detection MUST be performed.

Either side may tear the Softwire down with a StopCCN message, with no Softwire-specific action.
sections.eli5: First you knock and the hub opens the door (the tunnel). Next you agree on how to talk inside (PPP) and get a house number. Last, if you want, you ask for extras like a street map.

sections.title: Addresses, Prefixes and Keepalives
sections.content:
Several sections cover practices that are not required for interoperability. For IPv6, one /64 should be assigned to the Softwire to address both endpoints, preferably globally routable (Unique Local Addresses may be used in a private network). Delegated IPv6 prefixes are between /48 and /64 in length. An SI that gets a single /64 and has more than one interface is expected to bridge. For IPv4, the endpoints use host addresses (/32) negotiated by IPCP, and delegated IPv4 prefixes are between /8 and /30. Delegating a private IPv4 prefix is discouraged because it can cause nested NAT.

When the SC delegates a prefix, it SHOULD inject a route for it so traffic reaches the right Softwire. A Softwire can give stable addresses, and an SC should give a reconnecting user the same address and prefix. Addresses are expected to change if the user reconnects to a different SC.

For liveness, the SI and SC MUST periodically send a message to detect failure and keep NAT/NAPT state alive. L2TPv2 HELLO is the default tool, and the RFC-2661 defaults could mean 83 seconds to detect a dead end. Implementations MAY add PPP LCP Echo, with a re-emission timer lower than HELLO's.

The PPP MTU SHOULD be the link MTU minus the IP, UDP, L2TPv2 and PPP headers. On a 1500-byte IPv4 link that could typically be 1460 bytes, and lower still when IPsec is used.
sections.eli5: The hub hands each house a street number, and maybe a whole block of numbers for the rooms inside. It also pokes the house every so often to check someone is still home.

sections.title: RADIUS, Accounting and Management
sections.content:
The SC is expected to act as a client of an AAA server such as RADIUS. During PPP authentication, the server can return attributes in an Access-Accept message that shape the Softwire. The SC may include Tunnel-Type and Tunnel-Medium-Type in its Access-Request as a hint of the Softwire type.

  • IPv6 endpoints: a Framed-Interface-Id is sent to the SI in the IPV6CP Configuration Request. A Framed-IPv6-Prefix is used in router advertisements, or a prefix is chosen from the Framed-IPv6-Pool.
  • IPv4 endpoints: a Framed-IP-Address is given to the SI during IPCP negotiation.
  • Delegated IPv6 prefix: the Delegated-IPv6-Prefix attribute must be used for DHCPv6 prefix delegation, and the SC must link the DHCPv6 request's DUID to the tunnel and user.
  • Delegated IPv4 prefix: RADIUS has no dedicated attribute, but Framed-IP-Netmask together with Framed-IP-Address can tell the SC to delegate a prefix and route it to the SI.

For statistics, RADIUS accounting and the L2TPv2 and PPP MIBs already exist. The RFC notes that operators may find it hard to tell the address family of traffic in RADIUS accounting.
sections.eli5: The hub can phone a front desk (the RADIUS server) to ask what each house is allowed to have, like its street number, and then follows the answer.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The design goals are to reuse already deployed protocols and to scale very well. L2TPv2 security considerations from RFC 2661 apply. This RFC adds three points:

  • L2TP tunnel authentication happens at setup and may limit DoS attacks, since the tunnel is authenticated before L2TP and PPP resources are allocated.
  • AVPs carry no sensitive data in a Softwire, so AVP hiding is not used.
  • PPP CHAP gives basic user authentication, and other methods may also be supported.

For privacy, integrity and replay protection, L2TPv2 can be secured with IPsec. The IKEv1 approach in RFC 3193, RFC 3947 and RFC 3948 MUST be supported, because deployed technology is strongly favored. A newer, incompatible IKEv2 solution is described in a separate document and is to be considered for future phases.
sections.eli5: The hub can check who is knocking before it opens any door, and you can wrap the tube in an extra lock (IPsec) if the things inside are private.
